messages:
incident-bot: ALERT • KV cache + continuous-batching regression detected (sev2)
incident-bot: metric: kv_cache_paging_rate ↑ 7x, batching_latency_tail ↑ 4x, error spike for mixed short/long requests. Dash: https://dash.redwood/incident/1939743210
Maya: seeing it on our dashboard too. tail latency for /generate > 10s on 3 nodes. paging IOPS spiked.
Ryan: rolling logs now — looks like a regression from last night's batch scheduler change (deploy: batch-window=50ms -> 150ms) + kv-cache hysteresis tweak.
Liu: confirmed. Continuous batching growth + reduced eviction frequency caused kv working set to exceed in-memory target, extra paging.
Anna: we have one customer on Dedicated reporting 504s (case #5482). Sales wants impact statement.
Sam: marking customers with SLA risk and drafting a brief. For now, can we get a mitigation that reduces read paging while keeping throughput?
Maya: immediate mitigations I recommend: 1) revert batch-window to 50ms for the affected pool 2) bump kv eviction rate to previous value 3) enable short-request prioritization on scheduler 4) temporary route critical customers to smaller sequence-optimized model.
Ryan: I can push a rollback to batch-config for the pool. Starting now.
Ryan: command: ```kubectl -n inference set env config/batch-scheduler BATCH_WINDOW_MS=50 --record```
devops-bot: deploy triggered by Ryan — rollout id: r-2026-03-15-02-15. Watch: https://deploys.redwood/r-2026-03-15-02-15
Liu: I'm going to increase kv eviction throttle: ```curl -X POST https://ops-api/kvcache/evict_rate -d '{"rate": "1.5x"}'``` then monitor paging iops.
Claire: I'll wire up a temporary fairness weight patch to favor short requests: set scheduler.short_priority=1.8 scheduler.long_priority=0.6
Claire: patch pushed to canary on 3 nodes. Observability: tail latency for short requests down ~30% on canary.
Maya: good. also enable prefix KV caching invalidation for large seqs to avoid cache blowup (runbook ref: /runbooks/kv-cache-paging).
Anna: support update sent to affected customer: "We are actively mitigating a performance regression affecting mixed workloads. We're rolling back a recent scheduler change and applying targeted throttles. We'll follow up with a timeline."
Sam: add a line: possible cause: batch-window increase + reduced eviction compounded with a small number of long requests that monopolized KV slots.
Ryan: rollback completed on pool-3. rollout finished, no errors. Monitoring: kv_paging_rate trending down.
devops-bot: rollout r-2026-03-15-02-15 succeeded on 8/8 pods.
Maya: good. keep an eye on pack-shed metrics — we saw pack-shed events when paging peaked. If pack-shed increases, we may need to briefly restrict long-request concurrency.
Liu: temporarily limiting concurrency for long requests: ```curl -X POST https://ops-api/scheduler/concurrency -d '{"long": 12}'``` applied.
Claire: fairness weights applied cluster-wide. Short req tail latency normalized ~40% and kv paging reduced ~60% after both changes.
Maya: customer impact summary: - Affected: small set of Dedicated customers on pool-3 and some hosted tenants during peak - Symptom: 5-15s tail latency, occasional 502/504 - Duration so far: ~45m from first alert to mitigation rollout - Actions: rollback batch-window, increase eviction rate, apply fairness weights, throttle long-request concurrency, route critical customers to fallback model.
Sam: I'll prepare a short post-incident note for Sales + CS. Include timeline, mitigation, and next steps.
Anna: CS: will follow up with customer in 1 hour with ETA and technical summary.
Maya: next steps for eng: 1) root cause postmortem — compare pre/post scheduler commit 2) add canary for batch-window changes 3) add automatic rollback (if kv_paging_rate > 3x baseline for 5m) 4) expand pack-shed visibility to oncall dashboard.
Ryan: cloning the failing commit and running replay tests now. If we can reproduce, we'll add a regression test to the scheduler suite.
Liu: also propose a KV-cache heuristic: evict_by_request_type so long requests don't evict short-request hot prefixes. Will draft a spec.
Claire: for immediate stability, I'd like to keep fairness weights live for 24h and then slowly ramp down if stable.
Maya: agreed. I'll own oncall through the next 2 hours, then handoff to Ryan. Handoff at 1939746810.
Ryan: I'll take the overnight window after Maya. Will monitor dashboards and the customer queue.
devops-bot: scheduled follow-up runbook check at 1939750000.
Sam: capturing action items into the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/1939743210/actions
Anna: CS note: "We applied a rollback and tunings; performance is improving; monitoring continues. We expect normal service within 2 hours."
Maya: closing immediate mitigation loop. If anyone sees recurrence, ping me and escalate to platform infra. :thumbsup:
Ryan: thanks all — good coordination. We'll follow up with a postmortem and risk mitigation plan.
Anna: updating the customer case now.
Sam: thanks team.
